clue.text: Stresses English politician has increases withheld initially

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
taken as written

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for increases is held back, dropping it

parts.note: to rise is to increase, so increases means rises

explanation.surface: A complaint that an English MP has quietly held back pay rises from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withheld initially' drops the R from RISES, leaving ISES.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to stress a point is to give it emphasis, underlining its importance.

clue.text: River language this writer's covering

indicators.note: the setter's possessive wraps round the language, which sits inside it

parts.note: the setter's own, so 'my'
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: A writer covering a river and the language spoken along it.
explanation.walkthrough: Erse is a name for the Gaelic of Ireland or Scotland; the Mersey is the river at Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mersey is an English river in the north-west, flowing into the Irish Sea at Liverpool.

clue.text: Shelter — haunt regularly visited

indicators.note: only every other letter of the word haunt is visited, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A shelter that is someone's haunt, one they drop by at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: A hut is a small simple building giving shelter, an example of the wider word.

clue.text: Not fully settled, Baronet rearing Irish daughter as water lover?

indicators.note: the word for settled loses its last letter, so it is not complete

parts.note: settled, as in calm and unmoving, means still

indicators.note: in a down clue rearing means rising up, so the abbreviation is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: An unsettled baronet bringing up an Irish daughter who loves the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not fully' cuts STILL to STIL; 'rearing' turns BT to TB.
explanation.definitionFit: A stilt is a long-legged wading bird of shallows and marshes, so a fond frequenter of water, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Thwarted potential immodesty as method of working's abandoned

indicators.note: potential suggests the letters of immodesty could become something else, so they are rearranged
the letters for method of working are abandoned from the mix

parts.note: MO, modus operandi, is a method of working

explanation.surface: Someone's chance of immodesty foiled once their usual way of operating is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: IMMODESTY without M and O leaves IDESTMY, which 'potential' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stymied is to be blocked or frustrated, a direct synonym of thwarted.

clue.text: Uninteresting second report

parts.note: a tale is an account or report

explanation.surface: A second report that is dull to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale news or jokes have lost their freshness, so they are dull and boring.

clue.text: Artist's husband, impetuous

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A painter's husband described as headstrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash and impetuous both describe acting hastily without careful thought.

clue.text: Flexible notary seals final approval

indicators.note: flexible letters can be bent into a new order

explanation.surface: An accommodating notary stamps the last sign-off on a document.
explanation.definitionFit: In the UK, a bill becomes law only after the monarch's formal assent, the last stage of sanction.

clue.text: Northern child introduced to stolen goods — it shouldn't happen again!

indicators.note: the two pieces are put into the word for stolen goods

parts.note: swag is slang for loot or stolen goods
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A northern boy caught handling loot is told never to do it again.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation sounds like a scolding; it is really a cheeky gloss on a final performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell performance is by definition the last one, never to be repeated.

clue.text: Gross stupidity to ignore fellow's contribution of thanks

indicators.note: the letter for fellow is ignored, left out of the word for stupidity

parts.note: fatuity means foolishness or stupidity
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: Gross stupidity to overlook a man's thank-you gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ignore' removes F from FATUITY, leaving ATUITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip given to a waiter or porter is a small sum handed over in thanks for service.

clue.text: Looking back, leaders in Yalta after war you noted acted carelessly

indicators.note: looking back means the string of letters is read in reverse
the leaders are the first letters of the six words that follow

explanation.surface: A historian looks back at the leaders at Yalta after the war, and finds they acted rashly.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials give YAWYNA, which 'Looking back' turns round. 'carelessly' is the last word, sharing nothing with the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Done anyway means done in a slapdash, haphazard fashion, without care.

clue.text: Loathe journalist's twisted examination

indicators.note: twisted means the two letters are turned round

parts.note: ED, editor, is the crossword's standard journalist
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Hating a reporter's warped exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to hate intensely, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Effort to persuade the Ontario Ten to reform?

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A plea to persuade ten Ontario figures to mend their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhortation is an urging or earnest appeal, an attempt to persuade someone.

clue.text: One having unrealistic hopes of island timber at first

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber
first written as 1st, with the numeral one shown as the letter I

explanation.surface: A dreamer whose hopes rest on island timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is 1ST, the 1 read as I. DEAL is softwood.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone guided by ideals rather than practicality is a dreamer whose expectations may be impractical.

clue.text: Distraught ringsider has shock treatment

definitions.note: treatment given to a shock, a thick mass of hair

indicators.note: distraught means in turmoil, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A ringside fan at a boxing match so upset they need electric shock therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock treatment' suggests electroconvulsive therapy; a shock is also a bushy head of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is a thick tangled mop, so cutting and styling it is its treatment.

clue.text: One content with Continent?

parts.note: reads like a riddle about containment, but means someone happy with mainland Europe

explanation.surface: Someone happily at ease with the European mainland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like a noun about what is inside; it is the adjective meaning pleased. The Continent, to Britons, means mainland Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover of Europe and the EU is pleased with, contented by, the Continent.

clue.text: Place for the other, entwined, lots even?

definitions.note: the other is British slang for sex

indicators.note: entwined letters are twisted together into a new order

explanation.surface: Lovers entwined, with lots of evenings together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other' is British slang for sex, as in 'a bit of the other'.
explanation.definitionFit: A secluded hideaway where lovers meet for romantic or sexual liaisons.

clue.text: Great achievements of French town, extremely decisive in support of Church

parts.note: Tours is a town on the Loire in France

indicators.note: only the extreme letters, first and last, of the word decisive are taken

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
CE, Church of England

explanation.surface: A French town proves extremely decisive in backing its church.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour de force is a feat of great skill, a masterly accomplishment; the plural is formed on the first word.

clue.text: Uncertainty about tree cover perhaps

indicators.note: about signals the two letters are turned round

parts.note: an if is a doubt or uncertainty, as in 'no ifs or buts'
the elder is a tree

explanation.surface: Doubt about whether a tree gives enough cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns IF into FI. 'cover' looks like shelter from a tree; in cricket, cover is a fielding position.
explanation.definitionFit: Cover is a cricket fielding position, so whoever stands there is an example of a player in the field.

clue.text: State of confusion in German world over lady leader

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: Welt is the German word for world
ER, Elizabeth Regina, a queen who led the nation

explanation.surface: A German world in turmoil after its female leader.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A welter is a confused mass or jumble, a muddle of things.

clue.text: Some deride march — encourage diplomatic move

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Mocking a protest march versus encouraging one, mixed reactions to a demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: A démarche is a formal diplomatic step or representation made by one government to another.

clue.text: Principal criminal using cocaine for time

indicators.note: using one thing for another means it replaces it
for marks the swap of one letter in place of another

parts.note: a thief is a criminal
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: The ringleader of a gang using cocaine to pass the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Chief and principal both mean main or most important, adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Implement of Green power, say?

parts.note: to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A Green party tool of power, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Green looks political; here it is the golf putting green.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course, a club for rolling the ball into the hole on the putting surface.

clue.text: Stars like revolutionary car

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the two letters are reversed

parts.note: e.g. means for example, so like
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: Stars of the screen likened to a radical little car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins is a zodiac constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Sail away protected by detective — capital!

indicators.note: the pieces are sheltered inside the letters for detective

parts.note: DI, detective inspector
a jib is a triangular sail
out means away, not at home

explanation.surface: A detective guarding a yachtsman as they sail off, which is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital!' poses as an old exclamation of approval; it is the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of that name is the seat of government of the East African republic sharing it.

clue.text: Frequently ring newspaper

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: Phoning a newspaper often.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT, the Financial Times, is a London newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or poetic word meaning often, as in oft-repeated.

clue.text: Surprise to see crazy coming back

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: nuts means crazy

explanation.surface: A shock to see a madman returning.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish or amaze someone, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Loss of our fee, rift developed

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: We lost our fee after a rift opened up.
explanation.definitionFit: Forfeiture is the loss of property or rights as a penalty.
